classes.name: Hepatitis C direct-acting antivirals
classes.description: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (Epclusa and authorized generic), glecaprevir/pibrentasvir (Mavyret), ledipasvir/sofosbuvir (Harvoni and authorized generic), sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir (Vosevi), elbasvir/grazoprevir (Zepatier).
classes.plainDescription: An 8 to 12 week course of pills that cures hepatitis C.

records.verificationNote: Epclusa 400-100 mg tablet read at PDF p.19: Tier 4, QL - 30 day(s). Harvoni, Sovaldi and Vosevi read at p.20-21 (Tier 4, QL). An Epclusa authorized generic is marketed in the US but is not printed in this document, so genericAvailable is true with boglActive false (no brand-over-generic preference shown). Mavyret (glecaprevir-pibrentasvir) and Zepatier (elbasvir-grazoprevir) do not appear in this document; not all-inclusive. Document says: "Kaiser Foundation Health Plan does not have a requirement for PA" (PDF p.6) and "does not have a requirement for Step Therapy" (PDF p.7). Drugs not listed are nonformulary; when a Kaiser or referral doctor determines one is medically appropriate and necessary it is covered by formulary exception (PDF p.7; decision within 72 hours, 24 urgent, PDF p.8). Completeness is ambiguous: p.6 defines the formulary as "the complete list of prescription drugs preferred for use and eligible for coverage" but p.2 says "not an all-inclusive list", so absence is not treated as exclusion. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: policy wording corrected; 2 named absent drug(s) added as nonformulary (exception route)]

records.verificationNote: Epclusa oral tablet 400-100 mg: Tier 2, PA, SP, QL (1 tablet per 1 day), page 53 (layout extraction; hepatitis C agent combinations section). Epclusa is the only hepatitis C DAA on the list. Mavyret (glecaprevir-pibrentasvir), Harvoni and its authorized generic (ledipasvir-sofosbuvir), Vosevi and Zepatier do not appear on the list or its index. Epclusa pellet packets (150 mg/37.5 mg and 200 mg/50 mg) carry the same PA flags and are a pediatric form of the same drug.
